declarations.what_was_read: ALL ELEVEN deposited page images of St Mary's baptismal register (chicago/reference/catholic-baptisms-1833-1835/S3HT-DHG9-*.jpg), read off the scans entry by entry: the title page, pages 1 to 19 of the book, and one stray later leaf. That is the whole baptismal section of 1833-1835 and it is contiguous — 57 entries, 267 named readings, and the book's own pencil tallies (1833: 19, 1834: 24, 1835: 14) agree entry for entry with the reading. Entries 1 to 11 of 1834 are NOT Chicago: they were written at Bear Creek, the South Fork of the Sangamon and Springfield, in Sangamon County, on St. Cyr's journey back from St. Louis, and those rows carry at_chicago: false.
declarations.what_was_not_read: One line: the sponsors of 1834 entry 4, which stood on the last ruled line at the foot of page 7 and falls outside the scan's frame. They are not illegible — they are not in the deposit. Two page-sides carry entries OUTSIDE the window and are declared rather than transcribed: one 1849 entry (no. 40) in Father O'Meara's hand at the foot of page 6, and a stray leaf of four entries numbered 130-133, dated 1837-1838 and faded almost past reading. Both are described in the records file's out_of_window block so a later run does not read them again as if unread.

They are NOT undeclared any more: T-0503 read them off the register's own eleven page images and declared all eleven under its own ticket in this file. What this page did not carry, the scans did.
